source: NaCCA Religious and Moral Education Curriculum for Primary Schools (Basic 1-6), September 2019, printed pages 10-11
teacher_guidance: Respect religious and cultural diversity. For early-life narratives, use stories actually taught by the teacher; the curriculum names leaders but does not provide full narratives here. Accept age-appropriate oral, written, drawn or performed responses.

indicators.content_standard: B2.2.2.1. Explain the importance of religious festivals
indicators.indicator: Demonstrate activities which take place during the celebration of festivals.

skills.description: Recognise the examples and vocabulary in the lesson.
Explain meanings and connections in an example.
Apply the lesson to a situation and justify a choice.
Communicate understanding through a performance, drawing or demonstration.

misconceptions: Confusing a festival with the religion celebrating it
Thinking every festival is celebrated in the same way
Treating role-play as permission to ridicule a tradition
spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

questions.prompt: Which is a Christian festival named in the curriculum?
questions.hint: It is also celebrated as the birth of Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: Christmas is listed as a Christian festival.

questions.prompt: Which festival is named as an Islamic festival?
questions.hint: It is celebrated by Muslims.
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr is listed under Islam.

questions.prompt: Which festival appears among the Traditional festivals in the curriculum?
questions.hint: Choose a festival from the curriculum's Traditional list.
questions.explanation: Odwira is listed as a Traditional festival.

questions.prompt: Name one Christian festival mentioned in the curriculum.
questions.hint: Both are listed under Christianity.
questions.explanation: Either Christmas or Easter is correct.

questions.prompt: Name one Traditional festival from the curriculum list.
questions.hint: Recall the Traditional examples.
questions.explanation: Any one of those listed festivals is accepted.

questions.prompt: Match: Christmas; Eid-ul-Adha; Damba. Categories: Christian; Islamic; Traditional.
questions.hint: Use the groupings shown in the curriculum.
questions.explanation: These pairings reproduce the curriculum's festival categories.

questions.prompt: Name two activities that may take place during a festival, according to the curriculum.
questions.hint: Think of the listed celebration activities.
questions.explanation: The curriculum lists merry-making, sharing, family reunion and worship.

criteria.description: Merry-making, sharing, family reunion or worship (any two)

questions.prompt: Describe one way family members may come together during a festival.
questions.hint: The indicator mentions family reunion.
questions.explanation: Family reunion is specifically listed as a festival activity.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows sharing during a festival?
questions.hint: Sharing means giving or enjoying something together.
questions.explanation: Offering food is a simple example of sharing; actual customs vary by community.

questions.prompt: Tell about a festival you have seen or heard about and name one activity people did.
questions.hint: You may choose Christmas, Eid-ul-Fitr, Odwira or another listed festival.
questions.explanation: Learners connect the curriculum to a witnessed or heard-of celebration.

questions.prompt: Which activity could happen at festivals from different religious traditions?
options: Every group using exactly the same rituals
All festivals having the same name
questions.hint: Look for a broad activity that can occur in different celebrations.
questions.explanation: Gathering and sharing can be common activities, although each festival has its own practices.

questions.prompt: A classmate describes a festival you do not celebrate. State one respectful way to respond.
questions.hint: Show interest without making fun of the tradition.
questions.explanation: Respectful listening supports learning about different traditions.

questions.prompt: Role-play a family reunion during a festival. Show people greeting one another warmly.
questions.hint: Use welcoming words and gestures.
questions.explanation: Family reunion is one activity named in the curriculum.

questions.prompt: Draw a scene from a festival and tell the teacher which activity it shows.
questions.hint: Choose one activity from the curriculum examples.
questions.explanation: The curriculum asks learners to draw scenes from festivals; artistic skill is not assessed.

questions.prompt: Explain one way worship may be part of a religious festival.
questions.hint: Worship is explicitly among the listed activities.
questions.explanation: The curriculum includes worship as an activity during festival celebrations.

questions.prompt: Your group is preparing a festival scene for class. How can you make the role-play respectful? Give two suggestions.
questions.hint: Think about dignity and accurate representation.
questions.explanation: Role-play should teach about activities without ridiculing a religion or culture.

questions.prompt: Why might people share with others during a festival?
questions.hint: Connect sharing with community and family.
questions.explanation: The curriculum lists sharing and togetherness as festival-related values and activities.

questions.prompt: Put these festival activities in a sensible order: greet visiting relatives; welcome them; share a meal.
questions.hint: People usually greet one another before sharing together.
questions.explanation: The task checks understanding of a family-reunion scene, not a fixed ritual sequence.

criteria.description: Welcome/greet relatives, then share a meal; accept reasonable order of greeting and welcoming.

questions.prompt: Name festivals from two different religious traditions and give one activity people may do during each celebration.
questions.hint: Choose from Christian, Islamic and Traditional examples.
questions.explanation: Learner classifies two festivals and applies the shared activity examples without claiming all customs are identical.

questions.prompt: Give a short presentation naming one Christian, one Islamic and one Traditional festival and describing one respectful way to learn about each.
questions.hint: Include a festival from each curriculum grouping.
questions.explanation: The response demonstrates recall, classification and respectful learning.

indicators.strand: Religious Practices and their Moral Implications
indicators.sub_strand: Festivals in the Three Major Religions

indicators.content_standard: Narrate the early life stories of the leaders of the three main religions
indicators.indicator: Narrate the story of the early life of the religious leaders in the three religions in Ghana.

activities: role-play important aspects of a religious leader's early life

skills.description: Recognise the examples and vocabulary in the lesson.
Explain meanings and connections in an example.
Apply the lesson to a situation and justify a choice.
Communicate understanding through a performance, drawing or demonstration.

misconceptions: Inventing biographical details not in the curriculum
Treating one tradition's account as the account of all traditions
Confusing a name in the list with a detailed narrative
spec.source_limit: This curriculum passage names leaders and asks for early-life stories but does not itself provide the stories' details. Teacher-provided approved accounts are necessary for factual narrative questions.
spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

questions.prompt: Which person is named in the curriculum as a Christian religious leader?
questions.hint: The curriculum names him among the three religions' leaders.
questions.explanation: Jesus Christ is the Christian leader named in the curriculum.

questions.prompt: Which leader is named for Islam in the curriculum?
questions.hint: Use the respectful title given in the curriculum.
questions.explanation: The curriculum names the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as the Islamic leader.

questions.prompt: Which name appears among the Traditional religious leaders listed in the curriculum?
questions.hint: The curriculum gives several Ghanaian traditional leader names.
questions.explanation: Okomfo Anokye is one of the names listed in the Traditional examples.

questions.prompt: Name one traditional leader from the curriculum list besides Okomfo Anokye.
questions.hint: Two other names appear beside Okomfo Anokye.
questions.explanation: Toha Zie and Egya Ahor are also listed.

questions.prompt: Match the leader to the curriculum grouping: Jesus Christ; Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.); Okomfo Anokye. Groupings: Christian; Islamic; Traditional.
questions.hint: Follow the order and labels in the curriculum.
questions.explanation: These associations follow the curriculum's named examples.

criteria.description: Jesus Christ—Christian; Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)—Islamic; Okomfo Anokye—Traditional

questions.prompt: The curriculum asks the class to narrate an early-life story. What source should you use for story details not printed in this passage?
questions.hint: Do not guess details that have not been taught.
questions.explanation: The curriculum passage names leaders but does not supply complete early-life narratives.

criteria.description: A story or source supplied and approved by the teacher or curriculum materials.

questions.prompt: Using the early-life story your teacher has taught, retell one event in your own words.
questions.hint: Say who was involved, what happened and when in the story.
questions.explanation: Learners practise retelling an approved account rather than inventing unsupported biography.

questions.prompt: Name one religious leader whose early life was discussed in your class, and identify the religion linked to that leader in the curriculum.
questions.hint: Use the curriculum's leader list and the teacher's lesson.
questions.explanation: Accept a correctly matched name from the curriculum examples.

criteria.description: Any taught leader correctly associated: Jesus Christ—Christian; Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)—Islamic; Okomfo Anokye, Toha Zie or Egya Ahor—Traditional.

questions.prompt: When narrating an early-life story, what should come first: introduce the person, tell the events, or state what was learned? Put these steps in a sensible order.
questions.hint: A listener needs to know who the story is about before hearing events.
questions.explanation: A clear narrative introduces its subject, recounts events and may conclude with a lesson.

criteria.description: Introduce the person, tell the events in order, then state what was learned.

questions.prompt: A learner adds an exciting event that the teacher's story never mentioned. What should the learner do?
options: Leave it out unless a reliable taught source confirms it
Present it as a fact anyway
Say every tradition tells the same story
questions.answer: Leave it out unless a reliable taught source confirms it
questions.hint: Stories should be retold accurately.
questions.explanation: The curriculum requires narration; learners should not invent biographical facts.

questions.prompt: Listen to a classmate narrate a taught story. Ask one kind question about an event they mentioned.
questions.hint: Begin with a question such as 'What happened next?' if that fits.
questions.explanation: Listening and asking relevant questions support communication and collaboration.

questions.prompt: With classmates, role-play one important early-life event from a religious leader's story that your teacher has approved.
questions.hint: Agree on the event and roles before acting.
questions.explanation: The curriculum recommends role-playing important aspects of a leader's early life.
questions.misconception: Using invented details or mocking a religious figure.

questions.prompt: What is one thing you should check before comparing two leaders' early-life stories?
questions.hint: Check the source and the person first.
questions.explanation: Careful comparison avoids mixing traditions or creating unsupported facts.

criteria.description: That both details come from stories or sources actually taught and that each is matched to the correct leader and tradition.

questions.prompt: Summarise an early-life account taught in class in two or three sentences.
questions.hint: Include the leader, one event and the main point.
questions.explanation: Assesses concise and accurate retelling based on the class source.

questions.prompt: A classmate tells an early-life story from a tradition different from yours. How should you respond?
questions.hint: Show respect while learning about another tradition.
questions.explanation: The curriculum supports respectful discussion and collaboration.

criteria.description: Listen respectfully and discuss the story without insulting the person or tradition.

questions.prompt: Draw one scene from an early-life story your teacher has taught. Label the leader and explain what is happening.
questions.hint: Use only details from the story studied in class.
questions.explanation: The task assesses comprehension, not artistic skill or invented detail.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to listen carefully when learning the early-life stories of different religious leaders?
questions.hint: Consider accuracy and respect.
questions.explanation: Careful listening supports accurate narration and respectful learning.

criteria.description: To understand each story accurately, avoid mixing traditions and show respect.

questions.prompt: Prepare a three-part oral story plan for a leader's early life: beginning, important event, ending. Base it on the version taught by your teacher.
questions.hint: Keep the events in the same order as the source.
questions.explanation: The response should be organised and faithful to the taught narrative.

questions.prompt: The curriculum names Jesus Christ, Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) and traditional leaders but does not give their full childhood stories on this page. What is the responsible next step before writing detailed quiz facts?
questions.hint: A name list is not the same as a complete biography.
questions.explanation: Detailed questions require a verified source for the narrative facts.

criteria.description: Consult the full approved curriculum resources or teacher-provided stories; do not make up details.

questions.prompt: Present a short introduction to one leader's early-life story studied in class. State the leader's name, the tradition associated with them, and one verified event.
questions.hint: Check the story source before presenting.
questions.explanation: Combines identification and accurate narration without adding unsupported biography.

indicators.sub_strand: Early Life of the Leaders of the Three Major Religions

indicators.content_standard: Narrate the early life stories of the leaders of the three main religions
indicators.indicator: Outline the moral lessons in the early lives of the religious leaders.
curriculum_examples: Discuss moral lessons from the leaders' early lives
Explain how to apply lessons in daily life

skills.description: Recognise the examples and vocabulary in the lesson.
Explain meanings and connections in an example.
Apply the lesson to a situation and justify a choice.
Communicate understanding through a performance, drawing or demonstration.

misconceptions: Naming a virtue without connecting it to a taught story
Assuming every leader's story contains identical events
Confusing perseverance with refusing all advice
spec.difficultyPlan: 5 foundational, 7 simple-use, 5 application and 3 challenge questions.

questions.prompt: Which is a moral value listed with the early-life indicator?
questions.hint: Choose a positive value in the curriculum list.
questions.explanation: Honesty is one of the values listed in the curriculum.

questions.prompt: Which value means continuing to try through difficulty?
questions.hint: Think of not giving up when a task is hard.
questions.explanation: Perseverance is a moral value named in the curriculum.

questions.prompt: Name one value from the curriculum that can be learned from studying religious leaders' lives.
questions.hint: Choose one positive value listed for this indicator.
questions.explanation: Any one of the listed values is accepted.

criteria.description: Respect, obedience, perseverance, endurance, honesty, cooperation, commitment, dedication or humility.

questions.prompt: Which action best demonstrates cooperation?
options: Working with classmates toward a shared task
questions.answer: Working with classmates toward a shared task
questions.hint: Cooperation means working together.
questions.explanation: Working together is an example of cooperation.

questions.prompt: Which action best demonstrates humility?
options: Listening and not boasting about being better than others
questions.answer: Listening and not boasting about being better than others
questions.hint: Humility includes modesty and respect for others.
questions.explanation: Humility involves avoiding boastfulness and treating others respectfully.

questions.prompt: Give one example of honesty a learner can practise at school.
questions.hint: Choose an everyday action that tells the truth.
questions.explanation: Honesty is shown through truthful and responsible actions.

questions.prompt: Your group has a difficult task and one member wants to stop trying. Which moral value could encourage the group, and what could you say?
questions.hint: Choose a value about continuing through difficulty.
questions.explanation: Perseverance and cooperation can help learners continue constructively.

questions.prompt: How can a learner show respect while listening to a story about a religious leader?
questions.hint: Think about considerate listening.
questions.explanation: Respect is demonstrated through attentive and considerate behaviour.

criteria.description: Listen without interrupting, speak politely and avoid mocking the story or tradition.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between hearing a moral lesson and applying it in daily life.
questions.hint: Give an action that puts a value into practice.
questions.explanation: The indicator explicitly asks learners to explain how they will apply lessons in daily life.

criteria.description: Hearing means learning the idea; applying means acting on it, such as telling the truth or helping others.

questions.prompt: Match each value to an action: honesty; cooperation; respect. Actions: tell the truth; work as a team; listen politely.
questions.hint: Connect each word to its everyday meaning.
questions.explanation: Each action is a simple example of the named value.

criteria.description: Honesty—tell the truth; cooperation—work as a team; respect—listen politely.

questions.prompt: A learner makes a mistake during a group activity. Show how humility and perseverance could help them respond.
questions.hint: Combine modesty with continuing effort.
questions.explanation: Humility helps learners accept correction; perseverance helps them continue trying.

questions.prompt: After discussing a leader's story taught in class, name one moral lesson and one action you can take at home to practise it.
questions.hint: Use a real detail from the class story.
questions.explanation: The curriculum asks learners to connect lessons from leaders' lives to daily life.

questions.prompt: Role-play a child showing honesty after accidentally damaging a classroom item.
questions.hint: Show the honest words and responsible response.
questions.explanation: The role-play demonstrates the value of honesty in an everyday context.

questions.prompt: Role-play a group showing cooperation while completing a class task.
questions.hint: Let each person contribute.
questions.explanation: Cooperation is demonstrated through shared effort and respectful communication.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner use evidence from the story before saying that a leader showed a particular moral quality?
questions.hint: Connect the value to an event or action.
questions.explanation: Moral interpretation should be grounded in the story actually studied.

criteria.description: So the lesson is based on what happened in the story rather than an unsupported guess.

questions.prompt: Draw a scene showing one moral value you discussed from a leader's early-life story. Explain how the scene represents that value.
questions.hint: Use one event or action from the class account.
questions.explanation: Assesses value comprehension and application, not artistic skill.

questions.prompt: Name one way to show dedication to a good task at school.
questions.hint: Dedication means giving steady effort.
questions.explanation: Consistent effort toward a worthwhile task demonstrates dedication.

criteria.description: Complete assigned work carefully, practise regularly or contribute reliably to a group.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to hide the truth about a classroom mistake. Which value should guide your decision, and what should you do?
questions.hint: Choose the value that means speaking truthfully.
questions.explanation: Honesty guides a learner to be truthful while responding constructively.

questions.prompt: A learner says perseverance means never accepting help. Explain why this is not necessarily correct.
questions.hint: Persistence and cooperation can work together.
questions.explanation: Perseverance does not require refusing guidance; collaboration can support continued effort.

criteria.description: Perseverance means continuing to make effort; a learner can accept useful advice and help while continuing.

questions.prompt: Give a short presentation linking one moral lesson from a leader's story actually studied in class to one action you will practise this week.
questions.hint: Name the story detail, the value and your action.
questions.explanation: This directly connects a studied early-life narrative to application in daily life.

indicators.sub_strand: Early Life of the Leaders of the Three Major Religions
